2608.30748.title: The Fragility of Jailbreak Robustness Across Operational States
2608.30748.paper_summary: Existing jailbreak evaluations typically characterize robustness using a single attack success rate (ASR) measured in a default configuration (the vanilla state). However, user-LLM interactions can induce diverse operational states beyond the vanilla state. In this work, we find that jailbreak robustness is highly fragile to operational-state variation: even when the attack remains fixed, changing only an ordinary system prompt not designed to affect safety can dramatically alter attack success rates. We systematically investigate this phenomenon across seven aligned models and three representative jailbreak attacks, observing substantial differences in ASR between vanilla and non-vanilla operational states. In one case, ASR increases by up to 56 percentage points (2% to 58%) solely due to a change in operational state. Remarkably, these increases occur even for attacks originally designed and optimized under vanilla-state evaluation. We further show that state-dependent robustness variation is systematically associated with differences in hidden representations along a refusal-related axis, and that projections onto this axis strongly predict jailbreak outcomes. Our results show that a single vanilla-state evaluation may not fully characterize jailbreak robustness, motivating evaluations that also examine how robustness changes across non-vanilla operational states.
2608.30748.paper_summary_zh: 現有的越獄評估通常使用在預設配置（原始狀態）下測量的單一攻擊成功率（ASR）來表徵穩健性。然而，用戶與大型語言模型（LLM）的互動可以引發超越原始狀態的多樣操作狀態。在本研究中，我們發現越獄的穩健性對操作狀態的變化極為脆弱：即使攻擊保持不變，僅改變一個未設計為影響安全性的普通系統提示，也能顯著改變攻擊成功率。我們系統地研究了這一現象，涵蓋七個對齊模型和三個代表性的越獄攻擊，觀察到原始狀態與非原始狀態之間的ASR存在顯著差異。在一個案例中，僅因操作狀態的變化，ASR增加了多達56個百分點（從2%到58%）。值得注意的是，這些增長甚至發生在最初設計和優化於原始狀態評估的攻擊中。我們進一步顯示，狀態依賴的穩健性變化系統性地與沿拒絕相關軸的隱藏表示差異相關，並且在該軸上的投影能強烈預測越獄結果。我們的結果顯示，單一的原始狀態評估可能無法完全表徵越獄的穩健性，這促使我們進行評估，還需檢視穩健性在非原始操作狀態下的變化。
